title: sdf water-water (identical groups), chained 6 times, with mapgr
purpose: Exercises `sdf` [@epsrmanual], the variant of `sharm` in which molecules are defined by atom types and distance criteria, so that fragments or groups spanning molecules can be analysed; here whole water molecules, accumulated over a chained run and mapped with `mapgr`.
fortran: `sdf_rev2.f`: `run_sdf` (keywords), `sdf` (atom-group search by type and distance, pair loop, averaged groups)
system: The EPSR-test configuration `200DMSO400Water.ato`: 200 DMSO (atoms S, C, C, O, 6 H) and 400 water molecules (O1, H1, H1; SPC/E parameters [@berendsen1987]), 3200 atoms at 300 K in a cubic box of side 33.12 Å, a model of the DMSO-water mixtures of Soper and Luzar [@soperluzar1992]. `sdf` computes the same spherical-harmonic coefficients [@soper1994,@graygubbins1984] as `sharm`, but its "molecules" are groups of atoms found by atom types and pair distances (first atom = centre). Groups O1 H1 H1 with pair distances 0.976, 0.976, 1.54 Å ±20 %, axes as for water in `sharm` (z to the H-H midpoint, y from H 2); identical central and second groups (the second-group distances and axes in the file are overwritten by `check_symbol`); l1, l2 = 0-2, l = 0-4, n steps 2 (38 coefficients). `mapgr` rebuilds g(r) along chosen directions and relative orientations from the coefficients (grtype 1 radial, 2 spatial, 3 full orientational).
inputs: Input files written by hand from the keyword tables (`setup_symbols_*`), one `keyword value` per line, ended by `q`; `200DMSO400Water.ato` copied from EPSR-test. `water.SDF.dat` (nr 100, rmax 10, `averagemol y`); `water.mapgr.txt`: two full orientational views.
verification: Six passes: calculation in pass 1 and in pass 6 (`nsumt 5`, averaged with the stored `.h01`), final `nsumt 6`. Compared: `.SDF.h01`, both xyz files, updated `.SDF.dat` and `.mapgr.g01` after every pass. Reference build: `sharm`/`sdf` were rebuilt with one comma inserted in the run-time title format (`'(1h(,'//il1fmt`), since gfortran 15.2 otherwise stops with "Missing comma between descriptors" before writing the coefficients; all other programs are the unmodified reference binaries. Also masked: characters 31-45 of the `*.mapgr.g01` data lines, the error column of `g_centres(r)`, which `mapgrquad.f` never sets (uninitialised in the Fortran, 0 in the port).
notes: Fortran quirk reproduced: the remaining (H-H) distance is checked with `zdiff = ytemp(i2) - ztemp(i1)`, so according to the README only 235 of the 400 waters are accepted as groups.
